pageTitle: AWS WAF Fraud Control account takeover prevention (ATP) rule group
whatThePageStates: This page documents ONE AWS Managed Rules rule group (VendorName AWS, Name AWSManagedRulesATPRuleSet, WCU 50). It describes the two inspection modes the rule group performs (request inspection, and response inspection which is CloudFront-only), lists considerations including an explicit exclusion for Amazon Cognito user pools, catalogues the labels the rule group and AWS WAF token management add to web requests, and ends with a two-column rules-listing table of the 11 named rules in the rule set with their descriptions, thresholds, rule action and labels. The only enumerable coverage claim is that rules listing: these 11 rules are what the rule group contains. The page makes no per-Region statement, no per-service matrix, and no Yes/No/Partial support grid.

features.statuses: 11 rows, all present/supported; 0 explicit No, 0 Partial; 11 = 11. Each row names a rule that ships in the rule group, so presence in the table is the only status the table carries. Read from the 'Rule action' field, all 11 are Block: UnsupportedCognitoIDP, VolumetricIpHigh, VolumetricSession, AttributeCompromisedCredentials, AttributeUsernameTraversal, AttributePasswordTraversal, AttributeLongSession, TokenRejected, SignalMissingCredential, VolumetricIpFailedLoginResponseHigh, VolumetricSessionFailedLoginResponseHigh (11 Block; 11=11). Within those 11, 2 are stated to run only for CloudFront-protected resources (VolumetricIpFailedLoginResponseHigh, VolumetricSessionFailedLoginResponseHigh) and 4 are stated to apply only when the request carries a token (VolumetricSession, AttributeLongSession, TokenRejected, VolumetricSessionFailedLoginResponseHigh). Those are conditions on a supported rule, not a No.
features.scope: Two stated conditions, not a full second axis. (1) Protected resource type: the two FailedLoginResponse rules are evaluated only in protection packs (web ACLs) that protect Amazon CloudFront distributions, and responses are never inspected for HTTP/3 (QUIC) traffic. (2) Token presence: four rules apply only when the web request has an AWS WAF token. There is no per-Region and no per-plan/tier dimension anywhere on this page.
features.reasoning: The axis is the individual rule inside one named managed rule group; the table's unit of claim is one row per rule name, and each rule name is distinct (no collapse). The supplied catalogue vocabulary has no term for a rule inside a WAF managed rule group: 'managedRuleGroup' would be the axis only if the page enumerated rule GROUPS, which it does not (it documents exactly one), and 'ipsRule' means a Network Firewall Suricata rule. So 'managedRuleGroupRule' is a NEW camelCase name coined for this axis rather than forcing a bad fit.

features.featureName: ATP rule group availability by protected resource type
features.statuses: 2 values, and only 2 are named anywhere on the page: Amazon CloudFront distribution = Yes and additionally the only resource type where response inspection runs ('For CloudFront distributions ... the ATP rule group inspects your application's responses'; 'AWS WAF only evaluates this rule in protection packs (web ACLs) that protect Amazon CloudFront distributions'); Amazon Cognito user pool = explicit No ('This rule group isn't available for use with Amazon Cognito user pools. You can't associate a protection pack (web ACL) that uses this rule group with a user pool...'), reinforced by the UnsupportedCognitoIDP rule. 1 Yes + 1 explicit No = 2. Every other AWS WAF protected resource type (ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, App Runner, Verified Access, Amplify) is ABSENT from this page and must not be scored.
features.scope: None as a second dimension. The CloudFront value carries a mode qualifier (request inspection everywhere the rule group is allowed; response inspection CloudFront-only, and never over HTTP/3/QUIC), but the page gives no Region, partition or plan breakdown for either value.
features.reasoning: This is a real coverage claim rather than an inferred one because both values are STATED in prose: one as an availability exclusion and one as an exclusive capability scope. It is deliberately recorded as 2, not as the full AWS WAF resource-type universe: this page does not enumerate protected resource types, so any count larger than 2 for this axis would be fabricated from another page.

shouldNotExtract: The label catalogues are not coverage: the client session label, the browser fingerprint label, the 2 token namespace prefixes (awswaf:managed:token:, awswaf:managed:captcha:), the token status label names (accepted, rejected plus its 4 sub-reasons not_solved/expired/domain_mismatch/invalid, absent), the 3 extra ATP labels (signal:credential_compromised, aggregate:attribute:suspicious_tls_fingerprint, aggregate:volumetric:session:token_reuse:ip), and the many label strings embedded inside the table's 'Description and label' cells including the unactioned medium/low and successful_login_response variants. Also not coverage: the console-experience banner at the top, the repeated 'This documentation covers the most recent static version release' note (it appears twice), the pricing note, the WCU value 50, the numeric thresholds (20 requests / 10 minutes, 15, 10, 6 hours, 30 minutes, 5 IP addresses, 65,536 bytes / 64 KB), the two bullets describing request vs response inspection, the links to waf-atp.md / waf-tokens.md / the changelog, and the entire 'See also' AI-coding-assistant / Agent Toolkit boilerplate.
coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The page names no Region, no partition, and no Region-availability sentence at all; any per-Region figure attributed to this page is fabricated. SERVICE: nothing as an enumerated axis. AWS WAF is the subject, and Amazon CloudFront and Amazon Cognito appear only as protected-resource endpoints, not as an enumeration of services covered. RESOURCE TYPE: only the 2 values stated above (CloudFront distribution = supported and the sole home of response inspection; Cognito user pool = explicitly not supported). The page is silent on every other AWS WAF protected resource type, so the honest resource-type count is 2, not the size of the WAF resource-type universe.
trap:
The single most likely misparse is harvesting labels as coverage items. The page contains roughly three dozen backticked label strings across the token-label section, the ATP-label bullets and the table cells; a parser that globs on backticks or on 'awswaf:managed:' returns a large count that measures nothing. Runner-up: counting the table's rows as anything other than 11 — the cells are long, contain
breaks and embedded sub-bullets (rejected has 4 sub-reasons; VolumetricIpHigh and the two FailedLoginResponse rules each list extra medium/low labels), so a row-splitter that keys on line breaks or on 'awswaf:managed:aws:atp:' inflates 11 into 30-plus. Third: treating this page as an enumeration of managed rule GROUPS. It documents exactly one group; a parser that sees 'AWS Managed Rules' and expects a group list will either return 1 or, worse, pull group names out of the linked changelog. Fourth: reading the UnsupportedCognitoIDP row or the Cognito exclusion paragraph as a 'No' entry in the rules listing — the rule is present and supported; the thing that is unsupported is the user-pool resource type. Fifth: reading the CloudFront-only and token-only conditions as Partial statuses in a tri-state grid; there is no tri-state grid on this page.
